tools.description: Did the deploy land: diff the Postgres schema between two environments (schema drift), optionally with row counts. Row-level data: data_diff; one environment's migrations: migration_status / ddl_status.
tools.name: compare_environments

tools.description: Is a Postgres table's data the same in two environments (staging vs prod, after a seed or deploy): row count plus an order-independent checksum. Schema differences: compare_environments.
tools.name: data_diff

tools.description: Apply a ddl_preview's raw-SQL DDL plan to Postgres. Re-plans under a database advisory lock and refuses (DDL_DRIFT) if the schema, the ledger or the files changed since the preview. One transaction per migration, stopping at the first failure. High risks from the preview must be listed in acknowledgeRisks — only after a human has agreed to them.

acknowledgeRisks.description: Risk codes from the preview's requiredAcknowledgements, confirmed by a human.

tools.name: ddl_apply

tools.description: Create an index, table or other Postgres schema change as a raw-SQL migration: validates it and writes the V<timestamp>__<name>.up.sql / .down.sql pair to POSTGRES_DDL_MIGRATIONS_DIR. Does NOT touch any database; never overwrites a file. Risks are reported for review, then enforced by ddl_preview. Not available with POSTGRES_DDL_EXTERNAL_LEDGER, whose files are the repo's own. EF Core instead: migration_add.

down.description: SQL that reverts `up`. Optional, but without it the migration cannot be rolled back.

name.description: Migration name: lowercase letters, digits and underscore (^[a-z0-9_]{1,100}$).

noTransaction.description: Write the -- mcp:no-transaction directive. Required for CREATE/DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY; the migration must then be one statement.

up.description: The migration's SQL. CREATE/ALTER/DROP/COMMENT ON, GRANT/REVOKE on a named object, and ALTER … OWNER TO an allowlisted role; no DML, DO, role membership or transaction control.

version.description: 14-digit UTC timestamp (yyyymmddhhmmss). Omit to use the next one.

tools.name: ddl_create

tools.description: Test a ddl_preview's raw-SQL DDL plan: runs it inside one transaction and rolls it back, to catch failures before ddl_apply. Takes real locks while it runs (bounded by lock_timeout). Non-transactional migrations (CONCURRENTLY) are skipped and reported as skipped.
tools.name: ddl_dry_run

tools.description: Plan raw-SQL DDL migrations against a Postgres environment and return an approval token for ddl_apply. File mode applies pending files (direction "up", optional target) or reverts applied ones newest-first via their .down.sql (direction "down", target required; "0" = all). Inline mode takes sql instead. Reports per-migration risks and which ones ddl_apply must acknowledge. Executes nothing; refused on read-only environments (prod).

allowOutOfOrder.description: File mode: allow pending migrations older than the newest applied one.

direction.description: File mode: "up" (default) applies pending migrations; "down" reverts applied ones.

label.description: Inline mode: a name for the ledger (^[a-z0-9_]{1,100}$).

noTransaction.description: Inline mode: run without a transaction (needed for CONCURRENTLY; one statement only).

sql.description: Inline mode: the DDL to run, instead of files. Same rules as a migration file.

target.description: File mode: 14-digit version (the NNNN prefix with an external ledger). Up: apply through it. Down: revert everything newer than it ("0" = everything).

tools.name: ddl_preview

tools.description: Which raw-SQL DDL migrations are applied, pending, edited since applied (checksum mismatch), missing from disk or out of order in a Postgres environment, read from the configured ledger (mcp_ops.ddl_history, or the repo's own table with POSTGRES_DDL_EXTERNAL_LEDGER). Read-only; works on prod. Requires POSTGRES_DDL_ENABLED. EF Core migrations: migration_status.
tools.name: ddl_status

tools.description: What columns does a Postgres table have: name, data type, nullability, max length and default, in column order. Foreign keys: get_table_relationships; null/distinct stats: profile_table.
tools.name: describe_table

tools.description: Foreign keys between Postgres tables — all of them, or those pointing from or to one table: which columns to JOIN on, and what a write or migration reaches. Columns: describe_table.
tools.name: get_table_relationships

tools.description: Is the Postgres database reachable: checks this server and PostgreSQL connectivity for one environment. SQL Server: sqlserver-mcp health_check.
tools.name: health_check

tools.description: Which Postgres environments are configured (dev, staging, prod…): each one's write capability and masked connection info. Pass a name as environment to the other tools.
tools.name: list_environments

tools.description: List the tables in a Postgres schema (default: public), names only. Columns: describe_table; row counts and column stats: profile_table.
tools.name: list_tables

tools.description: Add a new EF Core migration (dotnet ef migrations add) and return the generated paths to edit. Does NOT touch the database; apply it with migration_preview → migration_apply. Raw SQL instead: ddl_create.
tools.name: migration_add

tools.description: Apply EF Core migrations planned by migration_preview: the planned ones (dotnet ef database update), or the rollback to its targetMigration (dotnet ef database update <target>). Drift-guarded; verifies the schema afterwards.

acknowledgeRisks.description: Codes from the preview's requiredAcknowledgements (always EF_REVERT for a rollback), confirmed by a human.

tools.name: migration_apply

tools.description: Test pending EF Core migration SQL before applying it: runs what migration_preview shows one statement at a time inside a rolled-back transaction. Reports the failing statement; skips (and lists) statements that cannot run in a transaction, such as CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY.
tools.name: migration_dry_run

tools.description: Plan applying pending EF Core migrations to a Postgres environment: snapshots the current schema and returns the pending migration SQL delta plus an approval token for migration_apply. Full idempotent script available at profile:verbose. With targetMigration, plans a ROLLBACK instead: reverts every migration applied after it ("0" = all) via their Down methods; migration_apply then requires acknowledgeRisks including EF_REVERT.

targetMigration.description: Rollback: an applied migration id to revert back to, or "0" to revert every migration.

tools.name: migration_preview

tools.description: Which EF Core migrations are applied and which are pending in a Postgres environment. Requires POSTGRES_MIGRATION_ENABLED. Raw-SQL DDL migrations: ddl_status.
tools.name: migration_status

tools.description: Profile a Postgres table's data: estimated row count, per-column distinct and null stats, and a few sample rows. Same table across two environments: data_diff.
tools.name: profile_table

tools.description: Query a Postgres database: run one read-only SELECT (or WITH … SELECT) with bound params in a read-only transaction, capped by a row limit and a statement timeout; explain:true returns the plan and estimated cost instead. Changing rows: write_preview. MSSQL: sqlserver-mcp.

explain.description: Return the EXPLAIN plan + estimated cost instead of executing.

tools.name: run_read_query

tools.description: Commit a Postgres write previewed by write_preview, using its previewId + approvalToken. Returns a rollbackId for write_rollback, or null when the preview reported the statement cannot be rolled back.
tools.name: write_apply

tools.description: Insert, update or delete Postgres rows, step 1: dry-runs one INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE in a rolled-back transaction and returns a previewId + approvalToken for write_apply. Requires POSTGRES_WRITE_ENABLED; prod is always read-only. UPDATE/DELETE must have WHERE unless allowFullTable. Check rollbackSupported/rollbackNote: not every statement can be rolled back.
tools.name: write_preview

tools.description: Undo a Postgres write committed by write_apply, using its rollbackId. Restores each captured row independently; a row changed since the apply is reported, not overwritten. A partial rollback is retryable.
tools.name: write_rollback
